meta.description: LUNR analysis: Intuitive Machines is turning a record $1.8B backlog and a fresh $600M+ satellite win into a real space-infrastructure story, but a live $500M ATM and negative equity cap the upside.

verdict.summary: Intuitive Machines has outgrown the lunar-lander label: a record $1.8B contracted backlog, ~$1.2B of fresh awards, a $600M+ commercial satellite program and its sixth NASA CLPS mission now frame it as a diversified space-infrastructure prime. Revenue is compounding fast (~$490M TTM, +310% YoY) toward $900M–$1B 2026 guidance. The catch is structural: the company is still loss-making, carries negative book value, and is actively selling stock through a $500M at-the-market program. This is a backlog-and-squeeze momentum trade, not an investment on fundamentals, sized small, with dilution as the ceiling.

$600M+ commercial GEO satellite win + 6th NASA CLPS lander, genuine diversification beyond moon landers

Sell-side mean target ~$29 implies material upside if execution holds
whyAvoid: Live $500M ATM (June 3), a permanent share overhang that sells into every rally
Loss-making with negative equity: EBITDA -$74M, net margin -27%, book value -$1.71/share
Q2 2026 EPS -$0.16 missed the -$0.07 estimate, profitability keeps slipping

business.overview:
Intuitive Machines (LUNR) began as a lunar-lander developer, it put the first US commercial spacecraft on the Moon, and is now repositioning as a broader space-infrastructure prime. Its work spans NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) missions, lunar data relay and communications, orbital services, and, increasingly, national-security and commercial satellite programs. Intuitive Machines IR· août 2026

The 2026 story is the backlog: management reported a record ~$1.8B of contracted work and roughly $1.2B of new bookings in Q2 alone, including a $600M-plus multi-satellite communications program and selection by NASA's JPL for the IM-300-class EAGLE-VSWIR Earth-observation mission (targeting a 2028 launch). Revenue is compounding fast, but the business still burns cash and funds its growth partly by issuing stock. Q2 2026 Results· août 2026

technicals.setupNote: Price ($17.43) is holding just above the rising 20-day EMA ($16.84) after the backlog-driven pop, with a fresh MACD bullish cross and RSI a neutral 55, not extended. It sits below the 50-day ($18.45) and 200-day ($18.99), so this is a reclaim attempt, not an established uptrend. Clean levels: resistance at $20.31 (mid-Aug swing zone, session high $20.84) then $21.83–$22.46; support at the 20-day EMA, then the $15.5 breakout base and the hard $11.33 shelf. ATR $1.55 (~9%) means small position sizing is mandatory.

shortInterest.note: 27% of float short with ~3.7 days to cover can force a violent bid on continued contract wins, but the same crowd amplifies downside on any dilution headline or mission slip.

capitalStructure.note: A $500M at-the-market equity program (424B5 filed June 3, 2026, ten underwriters) is live, following a $175M private placement in February. With negative book value, growth is being funded by continuous share issuance, the defining risk here.

risks.riskSummary: A real, fast-growing backlog wrapped around a loss-making balance sheet that funds itself by selling stock. Upside is capped by dilution; downside is amplified by leverage, negative equity and a high-beta, heavily-shorted float.

riskCards.title: Dilution Overhang (the main risk)
points: Live $500M at-the-market program (424B5, June 3) sells into every rally
Second raise in six months, $175M private placement in February
Negative book value (-$1.71/share): growth is funded by issuing shares
riskCards.verdict: Structural ceiling on the stock. Any move toward $20+ likely meets ATM supply, sized into the targets.

riskCards.title: Cash Burn & Unprofitability
points: EBITDA -$74M, net margin -27%, gross margin just 16%
$367M cash vs $481M debt, reliant on capital markets
riskCards.verdict: Fundamentals do not support the valuation (EV/Rev ~6x on a 16%-gross-margin business); this trades on backlog and momentum, not earnings. Management does guide to positive full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA, but that metric strips out stock-based comp and the company stays GAAP loss-making with negative equity.

riskCards.title: Execution & Mission Risk
points: Space-mission revenue is lumpy and milestone-driven
A failed or delayed landing/launch resets the narrative fast
Backlog-to-revenue conversion is the whole bull case
riskCards.verdict: The $1.8B backlog is real, but binary mission outcomes make the path to it volatile.

tradeIdea.entryNote: Pullback to the rising 20-day EMA, actionable at spot, not a chase
tradeIdea.thesis: LUNR pulled back to its 20-day EMA after a backlog-and-contract-driven pop, with a fresh MACD cross and a neutral RSI, a clean momentum entry rather than a chase. A record $1.8B backlog, a $600M+ satellite win and 27% short interest give it both a fundamental catalyst and squeeze fuel. This is a speculative, small-size trade: the live $500M ATM caps the upside, so take profits into resistance and do not marry the position.
